facts.statement: Segisaurus is a small coelophysid theropod dinosaur measuring approximately 1 meter (3.3 feet) in length.
facts.quote: Segisaurus (meaning "Tsegi Canyon lizard") is a genus of small coelophysid theropod dinosaur, that measured approximately 1 metre (3.3 feet) in length.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Segisaurus was discovered in early Jurassic strata in Tsegi Canyon, Arizona.
facts.quote: The only known specimen was discovered in early Jurassic strata in Tsegi Canyon, Arizona, for which it was named.

facts.statement: Segisaurus was a primitive bipedal theropod roughly the size of a goose.
facts.quote: It was a primitive bipedal theropod roughly around the size of a goose.

facts.statement: Segisaurus was nimble and insectivorous, though it may have also scavenged meat.
facts.quote: It was nimble and insectivorous, although it may have scavenged meat also.

facts.statement: Segisaurus had a bird-like structure with a flexible, elongated neck and a stout body.
facts.quote: It was bird-like in structure, with a flexible, elongated neck and stout body.

facts.statement: Charles Lewis Camp initially speculated that the neck ribs supported a Draco-like patagium to improve movement, based on the initial misidentification of furculae as clavicles.
facts.quote: These furculae were initially thought to be clavicles, which led Charles Lewis Camp to speculate that the "splint-like" neck ribs supported a Draco-like patagium along the neck, to improve the animal's ability to move quickly.

facts.statement: Segisaurus is known only from the holotype UCMP 32101, which was a sub-adult specimen.
facts.quote: Segisaurus is described from the only specimen ever found, the holotype UCMP 32101, which was a sub-adult.

facts.statement: The holotype of Segisaurus was discovered in 1933 by Max Littlesalt in Tsegi Canyon, Arizona.
facts.quote: In 1933, Max Littlesalt, a Navajo Indian, discovered the holotype in Tsegi Canyon of the Navajo Sandstone of Coconino County, Arizona.

facts.statement: Max Littlesalt pointed out the fossils to archaeologists on an expedition after discovering them while keeping livestock in the canyon.
facts.quote: After discovering the remains, Littlesalt, who kept livestock inside the canyon, pointed out the fossils to archeologists who were on an expedition inside the canyon.

facts.statement: Charles Lewis Camp likened the posture of the discovered Segisaurus specimen to that of a "sitting hen".
facts.quote: When the specimen of Segisaurus was discovered, Camp likened its posture to that of a "sitting hen", due to the position the dinosaur's remains were in.

facts.statement: Segisaurus was described in 1936 by Charles Lewis Camp based on a fragmentary skeleton consisting of limbs, pelvis, and vertebrae.
facts.quote: Segisaurus was described in 1936 by the paleontologist Charles Lewis Camp, based on specimen UCMP 32101, a fragmentary fossil skeleton which consisted of portions of the limbs, pelvis, and vertebrae.

facts.statement: No cranial material was recovered from the Segisaurus specimen.
facts.quote: Cranial material was not recovered.

facts.statement: Some scientists questioned whether Segisaurus was a theropod because it appeared to have solid bones unlike the hollow bones of Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Segisaurus appeared to be closely related to the better-known Coelophysis, but unlike the hollow bones of Coelophysis, Segisaurus had solid bones. This caused some scientists question whether Segisaurus was a theropod at all.

facts.statement: A 2005 re-examination revealed that Segisaurus had hollow bones and that previously identified clavicles were actually fragmented furculae.
facts.quote: In 2005, a re-examination of the Segisaurus holotype revealed that contrary to reports it did in fact have hollow bones and that the clavicles were instead fragmented furculae.

facts.statement: Segisaurus has a humeral shaft with stronger torsion (~50 degrees) than that of Coelophysis.
facts.quote: the humeral shaft has stronger torsion (~50 degrees) than does that of Coelophysis

facts.statement: Segisaurus has a rectangular humeral deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: the humeral deltopectoral crest is rectangular

facts.statement: Segisaurus possessed three claws and powerful legs that were very long compared to its body.
facts.quote: Segisaurus poseía tres garras y poderosas patas, muy largas comparadas con el cuerpo.

facts.statement: Strikingly, a clavicle was found in the Segisaurus specimen, which is unknown in other dinosaurs of that era.
facts.quote: Extrañamente la clavícula ha sido encontrada, cosa que no se conoce en otros dinosaurios de esa época.

facts.statement: The holotype of Segisaurus was discovered in 1933 in the Lower Jurassic Navajo Formation at Cañon Tsegi, Arizona.
facts.quote: Este espécimen fue hallado en 1933 en estratos del Jurásico Inferior, en la Formación Navajo en el Cañón Tsegi, Arizona, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The first discovery of Segisaurus was made by Max Littlesalt, a Navajo native living in Cañon Tsegi.
facts.quote: El primer descubrimiento del Segisaurus fue hecho por Max Littlesalt, una nativa navajo dentro del cañón Tsegi.

facts.statement: Segisaurus was formally described in 1936 by the paleontologist Charles Lewis Camp.
facts.quote: Fue descrito luego, en 1936 por el paleontólogo Charles Lewis Camp.

facts.statement: Segisaurus is known only from a single subadult holotype specimen, UCMP 32101.
facts.quote: Segisaurus se describe a partir del único espécimen jamás encontrado, el holotipo UCMP 32101, que era un subadulto.

facts.statement: The complete adult size of Segisaurus may never be known because only a subadult specimen exists.
facts.quote: Es posible que nunca se conozca el tamaño completo de Segisaurus como adulto.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in a sandstone bed, suggesting the dinosaur was buried in a layer of sand and died there.
facts.quote: El holotipo Segisaurus se encontró en un lecho de arenisca, lo que sugiere que el dinosaurio había sido enterrado en una capa de arena y murió.

facts.statement: Geological features of the Navajo sandstone formation suggest Segisaurus lived in an environment resembling modern sand dunes.
facts.quote: Las características geológicas de la formación de arenisca Navajo sugieren que este género vivía en un entorno que se asemeja a las dunas de arena modernas.

facts.statement: No cranial material was recovered from the Segisaurus holotype.
facts.quote: No se recuperó material craneal.

facts.statement: A 2005 re-examination revealed that Segisaurus actually possessed hollow bones, contrary to earlier reports of solid bones.
facts.quote: En 2005, un nuevo examen del holotipo Segisaurus reveló que, contrariamente a los informes, de hecho tenía huesos huecos.

facts.statement: Segisaurus belongs to the parent group Coelophysinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysinae

facts.statement: Segisaurus is classified within the family Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Family: Coelophysidae

facts.statement: The specimen was found in calcareous sandstone deposited during the Pliensbachian to Toarcian stages of the Jurassic, approximately 190 to 174 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue encontrado en arenisca calcárea, que fue depositada durante las etapas Pliensbachiense al Toarciense del Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 190 a 174 millones de años.

facts.statement: Segisaurus lived from the Pliensbachian to the Toarcian stages, between 192.9 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Toarcian (192.9 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some scientists questioned whether Segisaurus was a theropod due to its solid bones, though later studies confirmed it was a coelophysoid.
facts.quote: Esto hizo que algunos científicos se preguntaran si Segisaurus era un terópodo.

facts.statement: Current reports state that Segisaurus is vital for understanding the evolution of early theropods.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con reportes actuales, Segisaurus es vital en la comprensión de evolución de los primeros terópodos.
